title: feat(ductwork): one tmux server per crew, born in its own scope
description:
## wish: one tmux server per crew, so one crash ends one crew

### why
- every crew on a grove shares the default tmux socket (`DUCTWORK_TMUX_SOCKET` empty → `/tmp/tmux-<uid>/default`). a server segfault ended every crew at once, ~110 times in hours, on the distro tmux 3.2a.
- dev-env-setup now pins tmux 3.5a on a grove and installs systemd-coredump (bundles `2.8.tmux`, `1.6.8.coredump`), and lingers every seat (`1.6.7.linger`). the server LAYOUT is ductwork's, so it lives here.

### outcome
- each crew starts its tmux server on its own socket (`tmux -L <crew>`), so a crash ends one crew.
- the crew server is born in the crew's OWN systemd scope, never inside another crew's pane. dev-env-setup's reaper (`1.6.6.abandoned`) kills a process whose spawner is dead, which is not its cgroup's oldest, and which is older than 24h. a server born in a pane is all three once that pane closes.
- a pre-swap 3.2a server and a 3.5a client share protocol 8, so an attach still works; a fresh crew server takes the pin.

### clamp
- a crash of one crew server (`kill -SEGV`) leaves every other crew server alive.
- a crew server's cgroup is its own scope, never a peer pane's.

from: uladkasach/dev-env-setup @ beav/fix-grove-crew-users-linger
